root_cause.text: ionic_create_cq() in the RDMA/ionic control path allocated struct ionic_cq_resp on the stack without zero-initializing it, even though some fields/padding (rsvd[7] and cqid[1] when udma_mask skips an index) were not always written before being returned to userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `struct ionic_cq_resp resp;` to `struct ionic_cq_resp resp = {};`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that `rsvd[7]` was “NEVER SET” and `cqid[1]` could be unwritten because the loop skips indices not present in `vcq->udma_mask`, leading to an 11-byte stack leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize the CQ response structure in ionic_create_cq to avoid uninitialized stack data being used or exposed.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration in ionic_create_cq was changed from an uninitialized `struct ionic_cq_resp resp;` to a zero-initialized `struct ionic_cq_resp resp = {};`.
intent_record.how: This ensures all fields of `resp` start with defined zero values, preventing use of uninitialized stack data if the structure is partially filled or later copied/read before every member is explicitly assigned.

candidates.rationale: This stack allocation leaves struct ionic_cq_resp uninitialized. Because some fields/padding were not always explicitly written before being copied back to userspace, this directly enables leakage of uninitialized stack data.

vuln_statements.explanation: This declares the CQ response structure on the stack without zero-initialization. Because not all fields were always written before being returned to userspace, uninitialized stack contents could be exposed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is visible directly in `ionic_create_cq()`. The function declares `struct ionic_cq_resp resp;` as an uninitialized stack variable, unlike other response structs in this file that are explicitly zero-initialized (for example `struct ionic_ctx_resp resp = {};` and `struct ionic_qp_resp resp = {};`). Later, only selected fields of `resp` are written: inside the loop `ionic_create_cq_common(..., &resp.cqid[udma_idx], udma_idx);` populates `resp.cqid[udma_idx]` only for enabled UDMA indices, and after the loop only `resp.udma_mask = vcq->udma_mask;` is assigned before `ib_copy_to_udata(udata, &resp, sizeof(resp));`. Per the root cause, if `udma_mask` skips an index then some `resp.cqid[]` entries are never written, and reserved/padding fields such as `rsvd[7]` are also not initialized. Because the whole struct is copied to userspace via `ib_copy_to_udata(..., sizeof(resp))`, this function contains the information leak pattern. There is no fix present here, because the response struct is not zero-initialized before partial population.
